title: Cyclone Murasu to cross Andhra coast near Ongole late Monday as severe storm, IMD says
dek: The IMD expects landfall between 11.30 pm on 2 November and 4 am on 3 November, with winds gusting to 120 kmph and a storm surge of up to 1.5 m. Bengal faces only light rain, but Kolkata and Haldia ports have raised their storm signal.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Cyclonic Storm Murasu was about 300 km east of Chennai and 400 km southeast of Ongole at 11.30 pm IST on Sunday, moving west-northwest at about 23 kmph with winds of 85-95 kmph gusting to 110 kmph, according to the India Meteorological Department's (IMD) national bulletin issued at 2 am on Monday, as summarised by the live tracker Transclew. The IMD expected it to become a severe cyclonic storm early on Monday. It is forecast to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ongole, between about 11.30 pm on Monday, 2 November, and 4 am on Tuesday, 3 November, with sustained winds of 100 to 110 kmph gusting to 120 kmph.

The IMD warned of a storm surge of 1 to 1.5 metres above the astronomical tide in low-lying areas of south coastal Andhra Pradesh at landfall, with the highest surge expected over Bapatla and parts of Guntur, Krishna and Prakasam districts. Murasu, a Tamil word for a drum, is the second cyclone to threaten the Andhra coast in a week, after Cyclone Arnab. There is still no weather warning for West Bengal, but the distant warning signal at the Kolkata and Haldia ports has been raised.

## Latest bulletin

In its 2 am bulletin, the IMD put the storm about 350 km east-southeast of Nellore and kept its landfall forecast unchanged, according to Transclew. It said gale winds of 65-75 kmph could reach the Andhra coast by Monday noon. The IMD has issued a cyclone warning, the third of its four stages, for the Andhra Pradesh and north Tamil Nadu coasts, and red warnings for Monday in Nellore, Prakasam, Bapatla, Guntur and Krishna districts.

The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority, in figures reported by South First, expects the storm to cross near Bapatla on Tuesday morning, which lies within the stretch named by the IMD. The authority forecast district-average rain on Tuesday of about 179 mm in Eluru, 163 mm in Krishna, 161 mm in NTR and 147 mm in West Godavari, with extremely heavy rain likely in 20 mandals, and warned of heavy inflows into the Budameru.

After landfall the storm is forecast to weaken quickly to a deep depression by Tuesday evening and a depression by Wednesday morning as it moves north over Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, according to the IMD Kolkata bulletin issued at 10 pm on Sunday.

The IMD's national bulletin issued on Sunday evening forecast heavy to very heavy rain at a few places and extremely heavy rain at isolated places over coastal Andhra Pradesh on 2 and 3 November, heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places in Rayalaseema and Tamil Nadu, and isolated extremely heavy rain in Telangana on 3 November. South Odisha may get heavy rain on 2 November and heavy to very heavy rain on 3 and 4 November.

Gale winds of 80-90 kmph, gusting to 100 kmph, are expected along and off the Andhra coast from Monday evening, rising to 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph, from Monday midnight until Tuesday noon. Winds of 60-70 kmph are likely along the north Tamil Nadu and Puducherry coast from Monday evening. Fishing is suspended along the Andhra coast from Monday morning to Wednesday afternoon.

The IMD has warned of local flooding, waterlogging, disruption to road and rail traffic, damage to thatched and kutcha houses, uprooted trees and damage to banana, papaya and coconut plantations, and asked authorities to move people out of vulnerable coastal settlements.

## Andhra Pradesh prepares

Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu cancelled a visit to Delhi planned for Monday because of the cyclone, his office said on X on Sunday afternoon. The state health department said on Sunday it had set up 1,688 medical teams, 116 relief camps and 13,165 emergency beds, and readied 733 ambulances and 721 mobile medical units, South First reported. It had identified 6,870 pregnant women due to give birth between 1 and 10 November, and 493 had already been moved to hospitals.

Officials estimate that between about 12,100 and 15,100 electricity poles across 12 districts are at risk, according to South First. The disaster management authority's helplines are 112, 1070 and 1800 425 0101. Figures for evacuations and the deployment of national and state disaster response teams in Andhra Pradesh had not been published by early Monday.

## What it means for Bengal

The Kolkata bulletin says there is "at present no weather warning for West Bengal" linked to Murasu, which it is keeping under continuous watch. Distant Warning Signal No. 2 has now been hoisted at the Kolkata and Haldia ports, up from the Distant Cautionary Signal No. 1 hoisted on Saturday, with sectional signals II and IV at Sagar Island. A distant signal warns ships leaving port of a storm far out at sea; it does not indicate danger to the port itself.

Light rain or thundershowers are likely in south Bengal on Monday and Tuesday, with light to moderate rain at one or two places in North 24 Parganas, Kolkata, Howrah, Hooghly and the Midnapore districts on 3 November, and dry weather from 4 November, the bulletin said. Habibur Rahman Biswas, director of the regional meteorological centre at Alipore, earlier told ETV Bharat Bangla that the five northern hill and Dooars districts may see light rain on Tuesday.

There is no fishing warning for the Bengal coast, but the IMD has advised Bengal's fishermen not to go towards the west-central and adjoining northwest Bay of Bengal or the south Odisha coast from 2 to 4 November.

## Odisha and the south brace again

Southern Odisha is still recovering from Cyclone Arnab, which brought extreme rain of up to 546 mm at Patrapur in Ganjam district and forced tens of thousands of people from their homes, Pragativadi reported. The IMD expects squally winds of 40-50 kmph, gusting to 60 kmph, along and off the south Odisha coast from Monday evening, rising to 50-60 kmph, gusting to 70 kmph, on Tuesday, with rough to very rough seas until Wednesday afternoon.

IMD Bhubaneswar has issued an orange warning for heavy to very heavy rain in Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Gajapati and Ganjam on 3 and 4 November, Argus reported. In Ganjam, NDRF and Odisha disaster response teams have been stationed in sensitive areas and schools will stay shut until 3 November, according to Pragativadi and The News Insight.

## What happens next

The IMD expects Murasu to approach the coast through Monday, with the strongest winds from around midnight until early Tuesday. Ports and fishermen along the Andhra, Tamil Nadu and Odisha coasts should follow the IMD's district and port warnings, which will be revised as the storm nears land. The Kolkata centre said its next update for Bengal would be issued on Monday.

## Key numbers

- Landfall: south Andhra coast between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ongole, between about 11.30 pm on 2 November and 4 am on 3 November
- Peak forecast wind: 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph
- Storm surge: 1-1.5 m above astronomical tide in low-lying south coastal Andhra Pradesh
- Distance from Chennai: about 960 km at 5.30 pm Saturday; about 420 km at 5.30 pm Sunday; about 300 km at 11.30 pm Sunday
- Named: Cyclonic Storm Murasu, 11.30 am IST, 1 November
- Bengal: no warning; Distant Warning Signal No. 2 at Kolkata and Haldia ports
